USE OF SDF FOR DENTAL CARIES MANAGEMENT E143 PEDIATRIC DENTISTRY V 39 / NO 5 SEP / OCT 17 References on next page. Application frequency The effectiveness of one-time SDF application in arresting dental caries lesions ranges from 47 percent to 90 percent, depending on the lesion size and the location of the tooth and the lesion. One study showed that anterior teeth had higher rates of caries lesion arrest than posterior teeth. 33 The effectiveness of caries lesion arrest, however, decreases over time. After a single application of 38 percent SDF , 50 percent of the arrested sur- faces at six months had reverted to active lesions at 24 months.13 Reapplication may be necessary to sustain arrest.

title: AAPD Clinical Practice Guideline on Silver Diamine Fluoride (Crystal et al., 2017)
context: Bagian "Application frequency" dalam Appendix II membahas protokol praktis untuk penerapan SDF berulang pada anak-anak dan remaja dengan karies, menunjukkan bahwa aplikasi lebih sering menghasilkan tingkat penghentian karies yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan aplikasi tunggal. Rekomendasi mencakup perbandingan dengan agen fluoride alternatif seperti varnish natrium fluorida dan strategi kombinasi untuk manajemen karies komprehensif pada individu berisiko tinggi.
text:
After a single application of 38 percent SDF , 50 percent of the arrested sur- faces at six months had reverted to active lesions at 24 months.13 Reapplication may be necessary to sustain arrest.

8,31-33 Annual application of SDF is more effective in arresting caries lesions than application of five percent sodium fluoride varnish four times per year.30 Increasing frequency of application can increase caries arrest rate. Biannual application of SDF increased the rate of caries lesion arrest compared to annual application. 33 Studies that had three times per year applications showed higher arrest rates. 7,31,33,34 Frequency of application after baseline has been suggested at three month follow up, and then semiannual recall visits over two years. 24 One option is to place SDF on active lesions in conjunction with fluoride varnish ( FV) on the rest of the dentition, or alternate SDF on caries lesions and FV on the rest of the dentition at three months interval to achieve arrest and prevention in high risk individuals.

title: AAPD Clinical Practice Guideline on Silver Diamine Fluoride (Crystal et al., 2017)
context: Bagian ini dari Appendix II (Practical Guidance) membahas frekuensi aplikasi dan protokol pemantauan SDF untuk mengelola lesi karies pada anak-anak dan remaja, dengan penekanan pada pentingnya evaluasi tindak lanjut dan manajemen faktor risiko seperti plak untuk memaksimalkan keberhasilan penghentian karies.
text:
varnish ( FV) on the rest of the dentition, or alternate SDF on caries lesions and FV on the rest of the dentition at three months interval to achieve arrest and prevention in high risk individuals.

35 Another study recom- mends one month post operative evaluation of treated lesions with optional reapplication as required to achieve arrest of all targeted lesions.35 Individuals with high plaque index and lesions with plaque present display lower rates of arrest. Addressing other risk factors like presence of plaque may increase the rate of successful treatment outcomes.33 Practical recommendation: If the setting allows, monitor caries lesion arrest after 2-4 week period and consider reapplication as necessary to achieve arrest of all targeted lesions. Provide re-care monitoring based on patient’s disease activity and caries risk level (every three, four, or six months).

title: AAPD Clinical Practice Guideline on Silver Diamine Fluoride (Crystal et al., 2017)
context: Bagian ini merupakan panduan praktis implementasi silver diamine fluoride (SDF) yang menjelaskan protokol pemantauan pasca-aplikasi dan manajemen risiko untuk anak-anak dan remaja dengan karies, termasuk rekomendasi frekuensi reaplikasi berdasarkan aktivitas penyakit serta pertimbangan keamanan terkait kerusakan pulpa dan lesi karies yang dalam.
text:
consider reapplication as necessary to achieve arrest of all targeted lesions. Provide re-care monitoring based on patient’s disease activity and caries risk level (every three, four, or six months).

Careful monitoring and behavioral intervention to reduce individual risk factors should be part of a comprehensive caries manage- ment program that aims not only to sustain arrest of existing caries lesions, but also to prevent new caries lesion development. Adverse reactions No severe pulpal damage or reaction to SDF has been re- ported. 7,36-38 However, SDF should not be placed on exposed pulps. T eeth with deep caries lesions should be closely monitored clinically and radiographically.

title: AAPD Clinical Practice Guideline on Silver Diamine Fluoride (Crystal et al., 2017)
context: Bagian "Adverse Reactions" dan "Esthetics" dari Appendix II Practical Guidance membahas efek samping potensial dan masalah estetika yang terkait dengan aplikasi SDF pada gigi berlubang anak-anak, termasuk risiko toksisitas, iritasi oral sementara, dan penerimaan orang tua terhadap pewarnaan permanen pada gigi anterior versus posterior.

Serum concentration of fluoride following SDF application per manufacturer recommendations posed little toxicity risk and was below EPA oral reference dose in adults.39 The following adverse effects have been noted in the literature: • Metallic/bitter taste.24 • T emporary staining to skin which resolves in 2-14 days.24 • Mucosal irritation/lesions resulting from inadvertent con- tact with SDF , resolved within 48 hours.7 Esthetics The hallmark of SDF is a visible dark staining that is a sign of caries arrest on treated dentin lesions. This dark discoloration is permanent unless restored. A recent study that assessed pa- rental perceptions and acceptance of SDF based on the staining found that staining on posterior teeth was more acceptable than on anterior teeth.

title: AAPD Clinical Practice Guideline on Silver Diamine Fluoride (Crystal et al., 2017)
context: Bagian ini membahas pertimbangan estetika dalam panduan praktis aplikasi silver diamine fluoride (SDF), menjelaskan bahwa meskipun pewarnaan permanen pada gigi anterior dianggap tidak diinginkan oleh sebagian orang tua, mayoritas tetap menerima SDF untuk menghindari prosedur anestesi umum yang lebih invasif. Potongan ini juga menyertakan rekomendasi untuk informed consent dengan foto dan catatan tentang kode billing serta variabilitas pembayaran asuransi untuk prosedur SDF di berbagai negara bagian dan penyedia asuransi.
text:

40 Although staining on anterior teeth was perceived as undesirable, most parents preferred this option to avoid the use of advanced behavioral guidance techniques such as sedation or general anesthesia to deliver traditional restorative care. It was also found that about one-third of parents found SDF treatment unacceptable under any circumstance due to esthetic concerns. T o identify those patients, a thorough in- formed consent, preferably with photographs that show typical staining, is imperative. 40 T o improve esthetics, once the disease is controlled and patient’s circumstances allow, treated and now-arrested cavitated caries lesions can be restored.35 Other considerations • Coding – D1354; Reimbursement for this procedure varies among states and carriers. title: Chairside Guide: SDF in the Management of Dental Caries Lesions (AAPD)
context: Bagian pengenalan dan seleksi kasus ini menjelaskan prevalensi karies pada anak usia 2-5 tahun di Amerika Serikat dan memperkenalkan silver diammine fluoride (SDF) sebagai agen penghenti karies yang efektif, sekaligus mengidentifikasi kriteria pasien pediatrik yang menjadi kandidat ideal untuk perawatan SDF termasuk mereka dengan risiko karies tinggi dan tantangan manajemen perilaku atau medis. Potongan ini menekankan bahwa hasil visual dari perawatan SDF adalah pengerasan dan penggelapan lesi, dan bahwa aplikasi berulang mungkin diperlukan untuk mempertahankan penghentian karies seiring waktu.
text: RESOURCES: SDF CHAIRSIDE GUIDE 678 THE REFERENCE MANUAL OF PEDIA TRIC DENTISTRY ( WWW.AAPD.ORG/RESEARCH/ORAL-HEALTH-POLICIES--RECOMMENDATIONS ) Chairside Guide: Silver Diammine Fluoride in the Management of Dental Caries Lesions * Dental caries affects more than 1 of every 5 children ages 2 through 5 years in the US. 1 Silver diammine fluoride (SDF) is efficacious in arresting caries lesions 2,3 and may be included as part of a caries management plan for patients. Caries lesions treated by SDF usually turn black and hard. Multiple applications of SDF over time may be necessary to sustain arrest. Case selection for application of silver diammine fluoride Patients with cavitated lesions who may benefit from SDF in- clude those • with high caries risk. • with behavioral or medical management challenges. • who may need multiple restorative treatment visits. • with teeth that are difficult to restore.

title: Chairside Guide: SDF in the Management of Dental Caries Lesions (AAPD)
context: Bagian ini menjelaskan kriteria seleksi pasien dan gigi yang sesuai untuk perlakuan silver diammine fluoride dalam mengelola lesi karies, dengan fokus pada identifikasi pasien berisiko tinggi dan lesi karies yang belum melibatkan pulpa dental.

• with difficulty accessing dental care. Criteria for tooth selection include • cavitated caries lesions that are not encroaching on the pulp and have no signs/symptoms of pulpal involvement (eg, unprovoked/lingering/spontaneous pain). If possible, radiographs should be taken to assess depth of caries lesions. • cavitated caries lesions on any surface as long as they are accessible with a brush for applying SDF .

context: Bagian ini menjelaskan kriteria pemilihan gigi untuk aplikasi SDF dan prosedur klinis awal, termasuk pentingnya informed consent mengenai efek samping estetik dan ketidakpastian durasi penghentian karies pada pasien pediatrik dengan lesi kavitasi. Potongan ini juga mencakup dosis keamanan SDF berdasarkan usia dan berat badan anak serta langkah-langkah persiapan gigi sebelum aplikasi.

(Orthodontic separators may be used to help gain access to proximal lesions.) SDF can be used prior to restoration placement and as part of caries control therapy.4 Obtaining informed consent—includ- ing outcomes such as permanent staining of treated lesions, potential staining of skin and clothes, and unknown duration of caries arrest (with possible need for reapplication) as well as the role of SDF within a comprehensive preventive plan—is recommended.5 Clinical application of silver diammine fluoride • Age and weight of the child, along with the number of lesions requiring treatment, should be considered when determining how many drops of SDF can be safely applied in one visit. One drop of SDF contains approximately 1.7 mg of fluoride and 8.5 mg of silver.6 • Remove gross debris from cavitated lesion to allow better SDF contact with decayed dentin.

title: Chairside Guide: SDF in the Management of Dental Caries Lesions (AAPD)
context: Bagian ini menjelaskan prosedur klinis aplikasi silver diammine fluoride (SDF) pada lesi karies, termasuk dosis, persiapan lesi, teknik isolasi, dan metode aplikasi dengan microbrush untuk memastikan kontak optimal dengan dentin yang terkena dan meminimalkan efek samping pada jaringan lunak pada pasien anak-anak. Panduan ini menekankan pertimbangan estetika dan pencegahan pewarnaan yang tidak disengaja pada gigi tetap yang berdekatan.
text:

• Carious dentin excavation prior to SDF application is not necessary. As caries excavation may reduce the proportion of the tooth surface that turns black, it may be considered for esthetic purposes. • A protective coating may be applied to the lips and skin to prevent a temporary henna-appearing tattoo that can occur if SDF contacts soft tissues. • Isolate teeth to be treated using cotton rolls or other isola- tion methods. If applying protective coating to surrounding gingival tissues, use care to avoid coating the surfaces of the caries lesions. • Caution should be taken when applying SDF on primary teeth adjacent to permanent anterior teeth that may have noncavitated (ie, white-spot) lesions to avoid inadvertent staining. • Bend the microbrush. Dip brush into SDF and dab on the side of the plastic dappen dish to remove excess liquid before application.

Petunjuk detail tentang penggunaan microbrush dan perhatian khusus terhadap noncavitated lesions pada gigi anterior permanen mencerminkan fokus panduan ini pada manajemen karies pada populasi pediatrik dengan berbagai tantangan kesehatan.

Carefully restrict direct application of SDF to only the affected dentin lesion. • Application time should be at least 1 minute if possible, making sure the SDF is in contact with all areas of the lesion (especially in large posterior lesions). title: FDI World Dental Federation: Carious Lesions & First Restorative Treatment
context: Dokumen ini merupakan pernyataan kebijakan FDI World Dental Federation yang menetapkan pedoman untuk pengelolaan lesi karies dengan menekankan pendekatan minimal intervention dan pencegahan, bukan hanya perawatan restorasi. Potongan ini memperkenalkan latar belakang revisi kebijakan 2016 yang mendorong perubahan paradigma dari perawatan bedah/operatif ke pencegahan, serta ruang lingkup dokumen yang mencakup gigi sulung dan permanen dengan fokus pada konsep penghentian karies dan teknik restorasi invasif minimal.
text:
Carious Lesions and First Restorative Treatment Published on FDI World Dental Federation (https://www.fdiworlddental.org) Carious Lesions and First Restorative Treatment [1] September, 2019 San Francisco United States Context In 2016, FDI approved a revised version of the Policy Statement on “Minimal Intervention in the Management of Dental Caries” (2002) which recognized that “an operative (‘surgical’) approach should only be used when specifically indicated, e.g., when cavitation is such that the lesion cannot be arrested, or when there are aesthetic or functional requirements1.” The aim was to encourage a shift from a restorative approach of dental caries management to the delivery of preventive dental medicine2. Yet in spite of this effort, uptake in daily clinical practice so far has been slow.

Scope This policy statement gives guidance on treatment of caries in deciduous and permanent teeth differentiating the concepts of caries arrest and minimally invasive restorative concepts.

title: FDI World Dental Federation: Carious Lesions & First Restorative Treatment
context: Bagian ini menetapkan ruang lingkup kebijakan FDI mengenai penanganan lesi karies pada gigi sulung dan permanen, bersama dengan definisi operasional yang diperlukan untuk membedakan tingkat keparahan lesion (initial, moderate, severe) dan statusnya (active, inactive) sesuai dengan sistem ICDAS, serta prinsip fundamental yang menekankan peran edukasi pasien dan manajemen biofilm dalam penatalaksanaan karies. Definisi-definisi ini menjadi dasar untuk membimbing keputusan klinis mengenai kapan intervensi restoratif minimal invasif diperlukan versus pendekatan preventif berupa arrest karies.
text:
slow.

Scope This policy statement gives guidance on treatment of caries in deciduous and permanent teeth differentiating the concepts of caries arrest and minimally invasive restorative concepts.

Definitions (See also ICDAS system) Initial carious lesion: Non-cavitated carious lesion limited to visual change in enamel colour and texture Moderate carious lesion: Carious lesion limited to the outer third of dentine and micro cavitated carious lesions Severe carious lesion: Carious lesion extending beyond the outer third of dentine and cavitated carious lesions Active carious lesion: Carious lesion exhibiting net mineral loss over a period of time indicating that the lesion is progressing Inactive carious lesion: Carious lesion exhibiting no net mineral loss over a period of time indicating that the lesion is not progressing Principles It is fundamental to good practice that patients receive appropriate dietary advice and education about effective biofilm management.

Carious Lesions and First Restorative Treatment Published on FDI World Dental Federation (https://www.fdiworlddental.org) FDI World Dental Federation supports a shift in caries management from restorative treatment to measures that arrest and prevent caries development including monitoring, following the concepts of International Caries Classification and Management System (ICCMS™). 2 All initial caries lesions should be treated by the use of topical fluoride and monitored for progression. Further options are the use of fissure sealant in occlusal lesions and may include resin infiltration in proximal lesions into the outer third of the dentine3. In patients who cannot cooperate with treatment, silver diamine fluoride can be an intermediate alternative3-5. Follow up is essential in all cases.

In cases of progressive cavitation in deeper dentine, restorative treatment based on minimally invasive dentistry and selective caries removal should be considered. All treatments must also be accompanied by control of biofilm and use of topical fluoride in addition to patient education and patient follow-up. Clinical diagnosis of the activity of the carious lesion should take into account the location of the lesion, the surface appearance and careful tactile assessment as well as gingival health. Type and extent of interventions depends on the patient´s individual risk profile4,5.

Initial to moderate active or inactive carious lesions do not normally require tissue removal in the following situations: occlusal surface: fissure caries restricted to enamel; proximal surface: non-cavitated carious lesions limited to enamel and the outer third of dentine; smooth surface: non-cavitated carious lesions limited to the outer third of dentine and micro cavitated lesions. Lesions should be monitored during treatment and at regular intervals thereafter. Moderate to severe inactive carious lesions do not require tissue removal in the following situations: proximal surface: cavitated lesions in enamel when no tooth or prosthesis contacts the lesion; smooth surface: cavitated lesions in enamel and dentine when there is no aesthetic implication or any prosthesis clasp contacts the lesion.

text: FDI POLICY STATEMENT Caries management with Silver Diamine Fluoride Adopted by the FDI General Assembly: 2025, Shanghai, China CONTEXT Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) application is a minimally invasive treatment for caries, and it possesses both antimicrobial and remineralizing properties. Its a pplication (38% concentration) effectively arrests dental caries progression without adversely affecting the dental pulp. This non- restorative approach of caries management is simple, non-invasive and cost-effective. Additionally, it does not generate aerosols, thus minimizing the risk of cross- infection. SDF therapy is versatile , successfully arresting caries in both primary and permanent teeth, making it suitable for use in dental clinics, community health programmes and remote settings.

Potongan ini juga menekankan pentingnya diagnosis awal oleh dokter gigi dan pelatihan profesional kesehatan mulut untuk memperluas aksesibilitas terapi SDF sambil tetap mempertahankan standar keselamatan pasien.

Furthermore, oral health professionals can be trained to administer SDF under the supervision of dentists, thereby expanding its accessibility. However, dentists should first diagnose cavitated dentine lesions before SDF is used to arrest carious lesions, especially when the lesions are deep and close to the dental pulp. It offers benefits for young children, older adults , patients who have undergone head-neck radiotherapy and those with special care needs who may not tolerate traditional restorative treatments. DEFINITION Minimally invasive treatment in dentistry represents a holistic, team-based approach focused on preserving long-term oral health through preventive, patient -centred, behaviour-related care plans, that incorporate behavio ural guidance and attentive management of patients' needs, desires and expectations. The concept of minimally invasive treatment for dental caries management is to conserve remineralizable and intact tooth tissue to help retain teeth throughout life. Tooth tissue should not be removed unnecessarily. Its key components include early detection of lesions with caries risk assessment, remineralization of demineralized enamel and dentin, proactive measures to maintain healthy teeth, customized recall schedules, minimally invasive operative techniques to preserv e tooth structure, and repair rather than replace defective restorations.

PRINCIPLES • Prioritizing minimally invasive treatments for dentistry : to maintain oral health and effectively manage dental caries while reducing the need for invasive treatments.

• Personalized approach of d ental care: dental care that emphasizes individualized treatment and patient -centered strategies, considering their age, health status, and personal circumstances. • Accessibility and a ffordability: dental treatment should be accessible and affordable for all populations, particularly for vulnerable groups such as young children, older adults, and individuals with special needs. • Evidence-based practice: dental practices should be grounded on the best available scientific evidence. POLICY FDI World Dental Federation supports the: • Adoption of SDF as a minimally invasive treatment strategy for managing dental caries. • Use of SDF for managing dental caries in vulnerable populations, such as young children, older adults, and individuals with disabilities, and residents of facilities with poor access to dental care and those in remote regions.

CLINICAL INDICATIONS SDF is indicated for active cavitated carious lesions not encroaching on the pulp, especially where: • Behavioural or medical factors complicate restorative treatment. • Access to dental care is limited. SAFETY A territory-wide community service in Hong Kong performed more than 230,000 SDF therapy on children aged 3 to 6 years with no significant adverse effects. A laboratory study reported that the topical application of a 38% SDF solution delivered approximately 50% less fluoride than a 5% NaF varnish. Pulpa vital yang sehat bertanggung jawab terhadap pembentukan dentin sekunder, dentin peritubular, dan dentin reparatif terhadap respon biologis dan stimuli patologis. Pulpa dan dentin merupakan suatu kesatuan kompleks pulpa dentin, dimana jaring an pulpa menjaga kelembapan dentin, mempertahankan dentin tetap elastis dan kuat. title: PNPK Penyakit Jaringan Pulpa dan Periradikuler (Kemenkes RI, 2024)
context: Potongan ini menjelaskan teknik perawatan pulp capping indirek dengan stepwise excavation, bagian dari manajemen pulpitis reversibel yang dirancang untuk mempertahankan vitalitas pulpa melalui penghilangan karies bertahap dan aplikasi biomaterial pelindung dentin. Prosedur ini merupakan alternatif konservatif untuk gigi dengan karies dalam tanpa eksposur pulpa, memerlukan beberapa kunjungan dengan interval beberapa bulan untuk memantau remineralisasi dan pembentukan dentin sekunder sebelum dilakukan restorasi permanen.
text:
Peletakan bahan biomaterial dilakukan diat as dentin affected. Bahan yang biasa digunakan pada teknik ini ada lah ba han liner Semen Ionomer Kaca (SIK)/Resin Modified Glass Ionomer Cement (RMGIC).

Perawatan kaping indirek stepwise excavation, pembuangan karies parsial dengan prosedur bertahap terdiri dari minimal tiga kali kunjungan dengan jarak sekitar enam sampai delapan bulan dan enam bulan. Kunjungan pertama dilakukan excavasi awal dan meninggalkan dentin yang terkena berdekatan dengan pulpa. title: PNPK Penyakit Jaringan Pulpa dan Periradikuler (Kemenkes RI, 2024)
context: Bagian ini menjelaskan patofisiologi pulpitis ireversibel dalam konteks mekanisme inflamasi akut pulpa, termasuk peran leukosit polimorfonuklear dan pembentukan mikroabses, yang menjadi dasar rasional untuk perawatan ekstirpasi pulpa vital sebagai prinsip utama tata laksana pulpitis ireversibel. Potongan ini merupakan bagian dari pembahasan etiologi dan patologi penyakit/kelainan jaringan pulpa yang menghubungkan proses patologis dengan pilihan perawatan klinik yang sesuai.
text:
darah kapiler dalam pul pa yang dapat menyebabkan sel pulpa mengalami nekrosis. Daerah nekrosis ini akan memancing leukosit polimorfonuklear dengan cara kemotaksis dan memulai reaksi inflamasi akut.

Selanjutnya akan terjadi fagositosis oleh leukosit polimorfonuklear. Setelah fagositosis, leukosit polimorfonuklear yang memiliki rentang hidup yang pendek akan mati dan melepaskan enzim lysosomal. Enzim lysosomal akan melisis beberapa stroma pulpa dan bersama dengan debris selular leukosit polimorfonuklear yang mati akan membentuk eksudat purulent (pus). Proses inflamasi ini akan menghasilkan mikroabses (pulpitis akut). Pulpa a kan memproteksi dirinya dengan membentuk dinding dari jaringan ikat fibrous disekeliling mikroabses tersebut. Oleh karena itu prinsip perawatan pada ko ndisi pulpa ireversibel adalah perawatan pulpa vital yaitu dilakukan pengangkatan jaringan pulpa vital atau ekstirpasi pulpa karena zona infeksi dari kondisi ini masih berada di dalam sistem saluran akar/pulpa. Kista Periapikal/Radicular/Cystic Apical Periodontitis Kista radikular adalah kista inflamasi yang terjadi karena perluasan infeksi dari pulpa ke jaringan periapikal di sekitarnya. Sering ditemukan pada rahang atas anterior. Pada gigi posterior mandibula, kista kecil yang terpisah dapat muncul dari setiap apeks gigi dengan akar lebih dari satu. Gigi yang merupakan as al kista biasanya tidak vital, dapat menunjukkan klinis berubah warna, retak, atau menunjukkan adanya kegagalan perawatan saluran akar. Masa kista tumbuh sebagai pembengkakan yang perlahan membesar. Saat kista bertambah besar, tulang yang disekitanya menjadi tipis dan menunjukkan struktur yang kenyal karena fluktuasi. Pada rahang atas, ekspansi palatal dapat terjadi pada gigi insisivus lateral rahang atas.

Terminologi yang digunakan untuk nyeri kronis dihubungkan dengan intervensi tindakan bedah. Nyeri kronis setelah bedah termasuk surgically induced neuropathic pain (SNIP), chronic post-surgical pain (CPSP), Post-traumatic neuropathy (PTN), post-operative neuropathic pain (PPNP) dan phantom limb pain. Gambaran nyeri CPSP antara lain: (1) nyeri; (2) hyperesthesia; (3) nyeri allodynia dengan stimulus non-noksious; (4) nyeri pada sentuhan/dingin/panas; (5) nyeri hyperalgesia meningkat terhadap stimulus yang menyakitkan; (6) sensasi yang berubah; (7) par astesia; (8) dysesthesia; (9) numbness.

context: Bagian abstrak penelitian ini merangkum tinjauan sistematis dan meta-analisis tentang prevalensi karies gigi pada anak-anak Indonesia, dengan menemukan tingkat karies keseluruhan sebesar 76% di antara 8840 peserta dari 27 studi yang menggunakan berbagai kriteria diagnostik termasuk indeks DMFT yang direkomendasikan WHO. Penelitian ini mengidentifikasi perbedaan signifikan dalam prevalensi berdasarkan metode diagnostik yang digunakan, tetapi tidak menemukan variasi substansial antara lokasi geografis Jakarta dan non-Jakarta atau status komorbiditas peserta.

There - fore, we aimed to provide an updated assessment of this prevalence while also investigating the influence of patient characteristics and methodological factors. Design: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis, including searches of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase from inception to August 24, 2023. We included 8840 participants in 27 studies reporting the prevalence of dental caries among Indonesian children. Results: The overall prevalence of dental caries was 76 % (95 % confidence interval: 71% – 81 %). Studies in which decay-missing-filled teeth (DMFT) criteria were used to diagnose dental caries were significantly more prevalent than studies using non-DMFT criteria (78 % vs. 64 %, P < 0.05). No significant moderators were identified for the study subgroup based on study origin (Jakarta vs. non-Jakarta) or comorbidity status (comorbidity vs. no comorbidity).

According to the 2018 Basic Health Research (Riskesdas) findings, the prevalence of dental and oral health problems in Indonesia was 57.6 % [ 5 ]. The decay-missing-filled teeth (DMFT) index, endorsed by the World Health Organization (WHO), serves as a critical oral health status indicator, facilitating the measurement and comparison of tooth decay rates [ 6 , 7 ]. This index evaluates decayed, missing, and filled teeth, thereby playing a pivotal role in analyzing, controlling, developing, and implementing oral health initiatives [ 8 ]. Children aged 5 years with a caries severity score of DMFT > 6 fall into the severe early childhood caries category [ 4 ].

Globally, prevalence of dental caries varies widely among children. The WHO estimates that dental caries frequency in 5 – 6-year- old children from countries with low and intermediate incomes is 60% – 90 %, whereas in high-income nations, 20% – 40 % of children in this age group are affected [ 9 ]. Regional and demographic differences have prompted studies in various countries to assess dental caries prevalence. In East Africa, a systematic review and meta-analysis revealed a dental caries prevalence of 40.98 % [ 10 ]. In Ethiopia, 65.5 % of 3 – 5-year-olds were reported to have dental caries [ 11 ]. These findings underscore the substantial burden of dental caries in these specific demographics [ 12 ]. In Indonesia, updating and improving data on the prevalence and severity of dental caries in children is imperative to facilitate efficient oral health policy planning and resource allocation. 2.

Study selection We included full-text prospective, cross-sectional, retrospective, and case control studies reporting dental caries prevalence in children, without including language restrictions. Titles and abstracts were independently reviewed and analyzed for eligibility by two reviewers (FH and LTY). Any discrepancies were resolved through discussion with a third investigator (HSB). 2.3. Data extraction and methodological quality assessment Two reviewers (F.H and LTY) independently collected data and addressed inconsistencies. Extracted data included author, pub - lication year, study origin and design, participant age, male percentage, body mass index (BMI), comorbidity status, diagnostic measurement, sample size, cases, and prevalence rate.

Selection, inclusion, and characteristics of studies As shown in Fig. 1 , we initially identified 8303 potentially eligible articles. Of these, 233 duplicates were removed. Following screening of abstracts and titles, 8023 records were excluded based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. In total, 37 full-text articles met the inclusion criteria and underwent further review. Of these, 13 studies were excluded, with the reasons detailed in Suppl. Table 2 . Additionally, one study was sourced from website searching. Ultimately, 25 full-text articles meeting the inclusion criteria were retained [ 15 – 39 ]. These studies comprised a total sample size of 8840 participants.

Prevalensi keseluruhan karies gigi ditemukan sebesar 76% dengan heterogenitas substansial antar studi, dan analisis subgrup menunjukkan bahwa studi menggunakan kriteria DMFT memiliki prevalensi signifikan lebih tinggi dibandingkan studi non-DMFT.

4. Discussion To the best of our knowledge, this systematic review and meta-analysis represent the first comprehensive investigation into the prevalence of dental caries among children in Indonesia.

Our findings reveal a persistently high prevalence of caries, with similar rates observed across sample locations (Jakarta vs. non-Jakarta). Given the rigorous methodology employed in this study, these findings warrant substantial consideration. Principal oral bacteria include both gram-positive and gram-negative species, along with aerobic and anaerobic strains. Changes in the microenvironment can disrupt the commensal flora – host interaction, leading to disease. Dysbiotic microbiota contribute to the development of caries and periodontal diseases [ 40 ]. Pathogenic bacteria, especially those forming biofilms, counteract beneficial bacteria action. Oral biofilm polymicrobial composition includes Streptococcus , Actinomyces , Lactobacillus , Veillonella [ 41 ], Neisseria , and Eubacterium [ 42 , 43 ].

Although biofilms can thrive under human homeostasis, they are also responsible for tooth caries and periodontitis, the two most prevalent oral disorders [ 44 , 45 ]. Caries was found in > 50 % of research subjects aged < 11 years, with qualifying age categories including toddlers (1 – 5 years), children (6 – 10 years), and adolescents (10 – 19 years) [ 4 ]. Education markedly influences knowledge accumu - lation, as higher education levels correlate with enhanced information processing and knowledge accumulation [ 49 ]. Furthermore, age encompasses intrinsic factors, such as experience, environment, and prior knowledge, contributing to an individual ’ s under - standing of health maintenance [ 50 ]. Unhealthy dietary habits, including consumption of high-calorie food, contribute to increased caries prevalence [ 51 ]. We found that males and females in the lower BMI categories face a higher risk of caries development, consistent with the findings of extensive surveys conducted in Guangzhou [ 54 ] and the United States [ 55 ]. Severe caries often leads to toothache, reducing children ’ s ability and willingness to eat, thereby diminishing their food intake [ 55 , 56 ]. Certain children may experience concurrent medical and mental health conditions, such as epilepsy and anxiety, respectively, akin to attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, a neuropsychiatric condition impacting brain functioning. Symptoms manifest in an in - dividual ’ s energetic demeanor, concentration issues, and engagement in impulsive behaviors. Moreover, mental health – related symptoms may contribute to malnutrition, subsequently affecting dental health.

Individuals with mental illness, especially those with severe symptoms, may struggle to adhere to consistent daily dental care routines and access necessary dental treatment [ 57 ]. Regarding caries severity assessment methods, 22 out of 27 studies used the DMFT index, whereas the remaining studies did not. The DMFT index, recommended by the WHO, measures caries prevalence based on cavitated caries lesions, making it the most commonly used dental caries index in epidemiological studies [ 58 ]. Early diagnosis of noncavitated carious lesions enables preventive measures, potentially preventing caries-related morbidity and reducing the financial burden associated with restorative or rehabili - tative dental care. The International Caries Detection and Assessment System (ICDAS II) incorporates both cavitated and noncavitated carious lesions with acceptable reliability [ 59 , 60 ].

Finally, in interpreting our findings, several limitations must be acknowledged. First, variations in participant characteristics and study details, including comorbidities, caries diagnosis criteria, and sample size, contribute to study heterogeneity. Second, owing to incomplete reporting of continuous variables, such as age and male percentage, in some studies, metaregression analysis could not be performed. Nevertheless, the use of rigorous study methods and a substantial sample size enhance the credibility of this meta-analysis. 5. Conclusions Our study highlights the persistence of high dental caries prevalence among Indonesian children, with consistent rates observed across urban and nonurban areas. Urgent implementation of dental caries prevention health promotion campaigns is warranted, alongside prioritizing early screening for dental caries. F. Hasan et al.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian ini menampilkan afiliasi institusional para penulis dan abstrak studi, yang menjelaskan bahwa penelitian ini menganalisis data dari Survei Kesehatan Nasional Indonesia 2018 untuk mengidentifikasi prevalensi dan faktor risiko karies akar pada 37.057 responden dewasa menggunakan pemeriksaan klinis dan analisis regresi logistik.

Faculty of Dental Medicine, Universitas Airlangga, Surabaya, Indonesia. 4 Department of Preventive and Public Health Dentistry, Faculty of Dentistry, Universitas Indonesia, Jakarta, Indonesia.

5 Department of Restorative Dental Sciences, Faculty of Dentistry, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong ABSTRACT Background: Root caries (RC) remains a global burden and is often found in older adults. Risk factors for RC can vary in different countries. Purpose: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and risk factors of RC in Indonesian adults. Methods: This study analyzed data from Indonesia’s 2018 National Health Survey, which included 37,057 respondents aged ≥ 15 years. The survey collected data on sociodemography, oral health practices, general health behaviors, and oral conditions. An oral examination was conducted to measure the number of teeth with RC, decayed, missing, or filled teeth, as well as bleeding on probing (BOP), attachment loss, pocket depth, and number of eroded teeth. Logistic regression was generated to estimate odds ratios and confidence intervals.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian hasil dari studi epidemiologi nasional Indonesia tentang faktor risiko karies akar (root caries) pada populasi dewasa, yang menunjukkan bahwa usia lanjut, pendidikan rendah, dan kondisi periodontal buruk merupakan faktor-faktor utama yang meningkatkan risiko karies akar. Data ini berasal dari analisis survei kesehatan nasional tahun 2018 yang melibatkan 37.057 responden berusia ≥15 tahun dengan pemeriksaan intraoral dan regresi logistik multivariat.
text:
or filled teeth, as well as bleeding on probing (BOP), attachment loss, pocket depth, and number of eroded teeth. Logistic regression was generated to estimate odds ratios and confidence intervals.

Results: The prevalence of RC was 59.4%, mainly occurring in participants aged >45 years. Those aged >60 years had 2.52 times (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.52; 95% confidence interval [95%CI], 2.26–279) the number of RC compared with those who were younger. The likelihood of RC was increased by having a lower education (1.47 times; AOR = 1.47; 95%CI, 1.28–1.70) and never visiting a dentist (1.64 times; AOR = 1.64; 95%CI, 1.22–2.19). Decayed, missing, or filled teeth were shown to increase the risk of RC, where more coronal caries indicated a higher risk. Those with BOP (+) and attachment loss of >3 mm had a greater risk of developing RC. Conclusion: The prevalence of RC was relatively high, occurring mainly in middle-aged and older adults.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian ini merupakan kesimpulan studi epidemiologi nasional Indonesia tentang prevalensi dan faktor risiko karies akar pada populasi dewasa, diikuti dengan definisi klinis dan patofisiologi karies akar yang melibatkan demineralisasi permukaan akar yang terekspos. Penelitian menganalisis data dari survei nasional 2018 dengan 37.057 responden berusia ≥15 tahun untuk mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor sosiodemografi, perilaku kesehatan mulut, dan kondisi oral yang berkontribusi pada penyakit ini.

Root caries in the Indonesian adult population reflects a complex interplay of multiple contributing factors, including sociodemography, oral health practices, general health behaviors, and oral conditions. Email: yuanita.rachmawati.fk@ub.ac.id INTRODUCTION Dental root caries (RC) is caries exposed on the root surface below or at the cementoenamel junction and is diagnosed by visual and tactile methods. Root caries is caused by demineralization due to fermenting carbohydrates by cariogenic bacteria, which produce acid on the exposed root surface.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian introduksi ini menjelaskan mekanisme patofisiologi karies akar dan menyajikan bukti epidemiologi global tentang prevalensi tinggi karies akar pada populasi berusia ≥45 tahun, termasuk data insidensi dari analisis meta-regresi. Potongan ini menetapkan latar belakang untuk studi berbasis survei nasional Indonesia yang akan mengeksplorasi faktor-faktor risiko spesifik pada populasi dewasa Indonesia dengan prevalensi karies akar yang signifikan.
text:
and is diagnosed by visual and tactile methods. Root caries is caused by demineralization due to fermenting carbohydrates by cariogenic bacteria, which produce acid on the exposed root surface.

Studies show that RC is commonly found in elderly people and has become more prevalent as average life expectancy has increased globally. 1 Several countries have reported a high prevalence of RC in people aged ≥ 45 years in the last 10 years, including Mexico (96%), Greece (38%), the United States (25%), Australia (77%), and Denmark (75%). 2 One meta-regression analysis reported an annual incidence and increment of decayed/filled root surfaces of 32.95% and 0.64, respectively, in follow-up studies lasting <2 years, whereas these values were 9.4% and 0.43 in studies with follow-up lasting >5 years. 3 As life expectancy increases and access to dental services improves globally, the number of natural teeth retained in the oral cavity is expected to increase.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian pengantar (introduction) ini menjelaskan paradoks epidemiologi root caries pada populasi lansia Indonesia, yaitu meskipun retensi gigi alami meningkat seiring dengan peningkatan harapan hidup global, risiko penyakit oral termasuk karies akar meningkat pada orang tua akibat penyakit sistemik dan penurunan fungsi organ. Root caries memiliki dampak signifikan pada kualitas hidup karena dapat menyebabkan nyeri dan kehilangan gigi, yang menjadi justifikasi pentingnya penelitian epidemiologis tentang faktor risiko karies akar di Indonesia.
text:

The RC index was 2.6, and the highest index was found in those aged >55 years (4.4). The average number of normal roots (i.e., exposed roots without caries) was 5.5, and the average number of root fillings (RF) was almost zero in all age categories. The ratio of root decay (RD) to normal roots was 1:2. These data show that RC remains a problem that must be addressed by the Indonesian government.

context: Potongan ini berada di bagian Pendahuluan yang mengulas faktor-faktor risiko karies akar yang telah diidentifikasi dalam literatur epidemiologi global, sambil menekankan relevansi temuan tersebut terhadap konteks demografis Indonesia yang sedang mengalami pergeseran populasi menuju peningkatan jumlah lansia. Bagian ini membangun justifikasi mengapa penelitian tentang karies akar pada populasi dewasa Indonesia menjadi penting mengingat variabilitas faktor risiko antar negara dan proyeksi pertumbuhan populasi lansia di Indonesia dalam dekade mendatang.

A review addressing the epidemiology of RC reported several associated risk factors, including age, gender, exposed root surfaces, coronal caries, residence status, tobacco use, sugar consumption, tooth-brushing behavior, denture wearing, streptococcus count, lactobacilli count, and xerostomia. 7 Other studies have also found betel-chewing, periodontitis, erosion, and fluorosis to be associated with root and coronal caries. 8 Therefore, the varying prevalence of caries reported by several countries may be attributed to their different cultures, behaviors, health programs, and, thus, risk factors. Currently, the Indonesian population pyramid is dominated by young adults, meaning that in the next decade, the elderly population will increase.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian ini menjelaskan latar belakang dan metodologi penelitian tentang karies akar di Indonesia, menunjukkan bahwa meskipun penelitian RC terbatas, data survei nasional 2018 dapat digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor risiko pada populasi dewasa Indonesia yang terus menua. Studi ini menggunakan desain cross-sectional dengan data dari Survei Kesehatan Nasional Indonesia 2018 yang mencakup informasi sosidemografi, praktik kesehatan mulut, perilaku kesehatan umum, dan kondisi mulut.
text:
behaviors, health programs, and, thus, risk factors. Currently, the Indonesian population pyramid is dominated by young adults, meaning that in the next decade, the elderly population will increase.

9 Although research related to RC in Indonesia remains limited, the data obtained from the 2018 national survey can be used to explore the factors that are associated with the occurrence of RC in the community. This study aims to describe the prevalence of, and risk factors for, RC in Indonesian adults based on sociodemographic information, oral health practices, general health behaviors, and oral conditions taken from national survey data. MATERIALS AND METHODS This study analyzes data from the 2018 Indonesian National Health Survey conducted by the Indonesian Health Development Policy Agency, which can be accessed with specific requirements and procedures via www. badankebijakan.kemkes.go.id. 6 The survey was conducted at the national level, with a cross-sectional and noninterventional design.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian Metode penelitian ini menjelaskan desain dan prosedur pengambilan sampel dari Indonesian National Health Survey 2018 yang digunakan untuk menganalisis faktor risiko root caries pada populasi dewasa Indonesia. Potongan tersebut merincikan pendekatan sampling bertahap dengan stratifikasi berdasarkan kesejahteraan dan pendidikan kepala rumah tangga untuk memastikan representasi yang beragam dari 30.000 blok sensus.
text:
can be accessed with specific requirements and procedures via www. badankebijakan.kemkes.go.id. 6 The survey was conducted at the national level, with a cross-sectional and noninterventional design.

Ethical approval for the study was obtained from the Committee of Health Research Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Islam Negeri Maulana Malik Ibrahim Malang (No. 21/EC/KEPK-FKIK/40/VIII/2023). The national survey’s target sample consisted of 30,000 census blocks derived from the National Socioeconomic Survey conducted by the Central Bureau of Statistics. Sampling was performed using a probability-proportionalto-size approach combined with systematic, linear, twostage sampling. In the first stage, all census blocks from the 2010 Population Census were implicitly stratified according to welfare strata. In the second stage, 10 households were chosen within each census block through updated systematic sampling, with further implicit stratification based on the highest educational attainment of the household head to ensure diverse representation.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian Metode penelitian ini menjelaskan prosedur pengambilan sampel dan karakteristik partisipan dalam survei nasional kesehatan Indonesia 2018 yang menganalisis faktor risiko root caries pada 37.057 orang dewasa berusia ≥15 tahun, yang dikategorikan menjadi tiga kelompok usia dan dikumpulkan melalui wawancara terstruktur dan pemeriksaan oral. Data yang dikumpulkan mencakup variabel sosiodemo­grafi, praktik kesehatan gigi, perilaku kesehatan umum, dan kondisi oral untuk mengidentifikasi risiko penyakit karies akar.
text:
within each census block through updated systematic sampling, with further implicit stratification based on the highest educational attainment of the household head to ensure diverse representation.

Each participant provided consent by signing an informed consent form and received compensation from the government for their participation. 6 The study included people aged ≥ 15 years, with categories of young adults (15–44 years), middle adults (45–59 years), and older adults ( ≥ 60 years) 10 ; edentulous participants were excluded. Finally, the number of samples analyzed was 37,057. The national survey employed a combination of structured interviews and oral examinations. Interviews utilized standardized questionnaires to obtain detailed sociodemographic and behavioral information. Sociodemographic variables encompassed place of residence, sex, age, and educational attainment.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian Metode studi survei nasional Indonesia 2018 ini menjelaskan pengumpulan data melalui wawancara terstruktur dan pemeriksaan klinis untuk mengidentifikasi faktor risiko karies akar dan kondisi oral pada 37.057 responden berusia ≥15 tahun. Potongan ini mendeskripsikan variabel yang diukur mencakup demografi sosial, perilaku kesehatan oral, perilaku umum, dan temuan pemeriksaan intraoral menggunakan standar WHO untuk mendeteksi karies akar, karies koronal, dan penyakit periodontal.
text:
utilized standardized questionnaires to obtain detailed sociodemographic and behavioral information. Sociodemographic variables encompassed place of residence, sex, age, and educational attainment.

Behavioral variables included oral health practices—such as consumption of sweets and carbonated beverages, toothbrushing frequency, denture use, betel chewing, and dental attendance within the preceding year—as well as general health behaviors, including tobacco use, alcohol consumption, and regular medication intake. 6 Oral examinations were performed using the World Health Organization (WHO)-stipulated form and protocol. Instruments for the oral examination included plane mouth mirrors, metallic periodontal probes, Community Periodontal Index probes conforming to WHO specifications, and several pairs of tweezers. 6 Data on RC, decayed, missing, or filled teeth (DMF-T), bleeding on probing (BOP), attachment loss, pocket depth, and tooth erosion were obtained from the oral examinations. Root caries is identified by observing and counting the presence of RD and RF.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian metode studi survei nasional Indonesia 2018 ini menjelaskan protokol pemeriksaan oral WHO yang digunakan untuk mengukur kondisi periodontal dan karies gigi, termasuk definisi operasional dan sistem penilaian untuk setiap parameter klinis yang dikumpulkan dari 37.057 responden berusia ≥15 tahun.
text:
bleeding on probing (BOP), attachment loss, pocket depth, and tooth erosion were obtained from the oral examinations. Root caries is identified by observing and counting the presence of RD and RF.

The value for RD corresponded to the number of exposed roots with unfilled caries, whereas the value for RF corresponded to the number of exposed roots with filled caries. The DMF-T index was used to count the number of coronal caries based on category (i.e., decayed, missing, or filled). The BOP data were obtained by looking at the bleeding in the gingiva 1 minute after walking probing was performed. Gingival bleeding was recorded with scores of 0 (no bleeding) and 1 (bleeding). Loss of attachment was obtained by examining the index teeth (namely teeth 17/16, 11, 26/27, 47/46, 31, and 36/37) and was measured based on the highest score when probing using the following scoring system: 0 (0–3 mm), 1 (4–5 mm), 2 (6–8 mm), 3 (9–11 mm), and 4 ( ≥ 12 mm). Pocket depth was measured by walking probing and recorded as scores of 0 (no pocket), 1 (pocket = 4–5 mm), and 2 (pocket ≥ 6 mm).

Penilaian klinis termasuk pengukuran kehilangan perlekatan, kedalaman poket, dan erosi gigi menggunakan sistem skoring terstandar WHO yang kemudian dikategorikan untuk analisis regresi logistik.

Tooth erosion was determined by observing the damage to the hard tissue of the teeth, which typically looks smooth and shiny, occurring in the enamel with or without involving dentin, and is not caused by a bacterial infection. context: Potongan ini menyajikan hasil deskriptif dari analisis chi-squared pada Tabel 1 yang menunjukkan prevalensi karies akar (RC) berdasarkan berbagai faktor sosiodemografi, perilaku kesehatan mulut, perilaku kesehatan umum, dan kondisi oral dalam survei nasional Indonesia tahun 2018 dengan 37.057 responden berusia ≥15 tahun. text:
of <0.05) were observed across all variables. Descriptively, it can be seen that increased age correlated with a higher prevalence of RC, with people aged >45 years showing a prevalence of >70%.

The prevalence of RC was higher in men (60.3%) than in women (58.7%). Root caries was more often observed in participants who lived in rural areas (62.5%), had lower formal education (69.5%), did not wear dentures (64.2%), and never visited the dentist (59.5%). Those who never ate sweets were more likely to have RC (62.7%), whereas those who consumed more than one sweet drink per day tended to have RC (61.1%). Participants who drank soda (52.7%), did not brush their teeth (65.6%), or took medicine regularly (66.6%) tended to have higher levels of RC than their counterparts. In terms of smoking behavior, respondents who smoked every day (64.3%), never chewed betel (59.4%), or did not drink alcohol every day (59.7%) had higher levels of RC than their counterparts.

Potongan ini melengkapi analisis bivariat yang menunjukkan hubungan signifikan antara faktor-faktor perilaku (merokok, mengunyah sirih, konsumsi alkohol) dan kondisi klinis oral (indeks DMF-T, bleeding on probing, kedalaman poket, kehilangan perlekatan, dan erosi gigi) dengan kejadian karies akar.

In terms of smoking behavior, respondents who smoked every day (64.3%), never chewed betel (59.4%), or did not drink alcohol every day (59.7%) had higher levels of RC than their counterparts.

Increased prevalence of RC was also seen in those with high levels of DMF-T (80.8%), BOP (+) (63.5%), pocket depth (68.3%), attachment loss (72.4%), and erosion (69.6%). title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian hasil penelitian ini melaporkan odds ratio yang disesuaikan (AOR) dari analisis regresi logistik multivariat yang mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor risiko perilaku, kesehatan umum, dan kondisi oral yang berhubungan dengan prevalensi root caries pada sampel nasional Indonesia berusia ≥15 tahun. Model regresi menunjukkan kecocokan yang baik dengan nilai Nagelkerke R² sebesar 0,293, menjelaskan bahwa berbagai faktor termasuk penggunaan obat rutin, merokok harian, dan kondisi periodontal seperti bleeding on probing dan attachment loss meningkatkan risiko root caries.

The risk of RC was also 1.20 (AOR = 1.20; 95%CI, 1.12–1.28) or 1.21 (AOR = 1.21; 95%CI, 1.09–1.35) times higher in those who were on routine medication or smoked daily, respectively. Those who chewed betel (72%; AOR = 0.72; 95%CI, 0.59–0.88) and drank alcohol (75%; AOR = 0.75; 95%CI, 0.60–0.92) had RC. Decayed, missing, or filled teeth were shown to increase the risk of RC, where more coronal caries indicated a higher risk. Those with BOP (+) (1.30 times; AOR = 1.30; 95%CI, 1.21–1.39), attachment loss of >3 mm (1.30 times; AOR = 1.30; 95%CI, 1.17–1.37), and erosion (1.12 times; AOR = 1.12; 95%CI, 1.02–1.24) had a greater risk of developing RC. The logistic regression showed a Hosmer–Lemeshow test value of 0.402, and the Nagelkerke R 2 value was 0.293. The results indicated a good fit for the model, as evidenced by suggesting that the model accounted for approximately 29.3% of the variability in the RC.

Penulis menggunakan data dari Survei Kesehatan Nasional Indonesia 2018, sebuah survei nasional berskala besar yang dilakukan secara berkala setiap lima tahun, untuk mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor sosiodemografi, perilaku kesehatan mulut, dan kondisi oral yang berkontribusi terhadap terjadinya karies akar.

DISCUSSION Root caries is a preventable disease with a good prognosis when detected early and treated promptly. 5 It is most prevalent in older adults; this situation requires strategies or efforts for prevention and treatment by identifying the risk factors of RC. In 2021, 27.9% of Indonesia’s population was aged >45 years, 39.6% were aged 20–44 years, and the average life expectancy was 73 years. 9 From these data, it can be predicted that in the next 5–10 years, the number of older adults in Indonesia will increase sharply. This study is expected to provide an overview of the factors contributing to the occurrence of RC in Indonesian adults so that government prevention programs can be developed based on the existing conditions. The research data were taken from the 2018 Indonesian National Health Survey, 6 which is conducted routinely every 5 years.

title: Understanding root caries risk in Indonesian adults: evidence from a nationwide survey
context: Bagian ini menyajikan hasil utama studi analisis data Survei Kesehatan Nasional Indonesia 2018 mengenai prevalensi karies akar (RC) sebesar 59,4% pada populasi dewasa berusia ≥15 tahun, dengan penekanan pada peran faktor sosiodemografi terutama usia sebagai determinan kuat terhadap RC. Potongan ini juga membandingkan tingkat RC pada lansia Indonesia dengan negara-negara Asia lainnya dan mengulas konsistensi temuan tentang hubungan antara usia dan RC dalam literatur epidemiologi.
text:
prevention programs can be developed based on the existing conditions. The research data were taken from the 2018 Indonesian National Health Survey, 6 which is conducted routinely every 5 years.

The data analyzed came from respondents aged ≥ 15 years. The results showed that the prevalence of RC was 59.4%, and on average, DMF-T was 8.56. Our results showed that many sociodemographic factors played a role in RC occurrence, including age, residence location, and education level. The association between age and RC becomes stronger with increased age, as does the risk of caries. The highest prevalence of RC was seen in those aged >60 years (74.2%). Compared with other countries in Asia, the rate of RC in elderly people in our sample was relatively high. For example, the RC prevalence in elderly people has been reported to be 43.9% in China 11 and 89.7% in Nepal. 12 In two reviews published in 2020, 5 out of 11 studies showed a positive correlation between age and RC, 2 as did 16 out of 25 cross-sectional studies. 1 However, several studies in the review did not report this positive correlation.

context: Bagian diskusi penelitian ini membahas mekanisme biologis dan faktor-faktor yang mendasari hubungan antara usia lanjut dan risiko karies akar (root caries/RC) dalam populasi dewasa Indonesia, termasuk peran penyakit sistemik dan penggunaan obat regular sebagai faktor kontribusi.
text:
5 out of 11 studies showed a positive correlation between age and RC, 2 as did 16 out of 25 cross-sectional studies. 1 However, several studies in the review did not report this positive correlation.

The high risk of RC seen in elderly people is attributed to several factors, such as decreased ability to maintain oral hygiene, systemic diseases, increased incidence of gingival recession, and low self-efficacy. 13 Systemic diseases that are thought to be associated with RC include cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Individuals with three or more RCs are twice as likely to experience cardiac arrhythmias, and the prevalence of xerostomia is 62% higher in patients with diabetes mellitus. 13 The data in this study also found that taking medication regularly was associated with RC. This association may be attributed to the higher rate of systemic diseases in elderly people, which will impact the occurrence of RC and can also be triggered by the drugs they take regularly.

Potongan ini juga menghubungkan temuan dengan konteks sosiodemografi Indonesia sebagai negara berpenghasilan menengah ke bawah dengan populasi yang tersebar di area rural dengan akses terbatas.

Participants who lived in rural areas exhibited a higher prevalence of RC, which agreed with the results of a systematic review, where two out of three cohort studies reported the same finding. 2 Communities in rural areas are more at risk of developing RC, possibly because access to healthcare facilities is more limited than in urban areas. The data supported this finding, as those who never visited the dentist tended to have more RCs. In terms of geography, Indonesia exhibits heterogeneity between rural and urban areas in terms of economy and distribution of healthcare facilities. As one of the most populated countries in the world, 9 and as a lower-middle-income country with a per capita gross national income of USD 3,630, approximately half of Indonesia’s population lives in rural areas with limited access to healthcare workers and a low level of welfare compared with urban areas.

14 Participants with a low education level tended to have a higher prevalence of RC. By contrast, in one review, no statistical correlation was found between RC and education level. However, descriptively, people with a higher education had fewer RCs. 1 One study from Mexico reported that an increased risk of RC was not directly associated with education level. 15 The authors argued that someone with higher education is typically associated with better socioeconomic and health literacy than those with low education; thus, their ability to maintain oral hygiene is also better, either independently or by visiting healthcare facilities. Our results showed that active smokers tended to have more RCs. This finding aligns with a review reporting that smoking and RC were correlated in 5 out of 10 studies, 1 as well as results from an Australian study.

These conditions encourage an increase in the number of pathogenic bacteria in the biofilm, resulting in caries. 16 This study found a strong positive correlation between coronal caries and RC. The main etiological factor in the early stages and over the course of RC in elderly people is the presence of bacteria and fermentable carbohydrates on the root surface of the teeth. Culturally, bacteria associated with RC include Lactobacillus acidophilus with Streptococcus mutans , Actinomyces israelii with L. acidophilus , and A. israelii with L. acidophilus and S. mutans . 17 One study from Turkey found that smoking also affected the occurrence of periodontal disease, 18 where the smoking group was more susceptible to advanced periodontal disease and at higher risk of bone resorption and tooth loss.

Potongan ini menjelaskan mekanisme biologi dan epidemiologis bagaimana kedua perilaku tersebut mempengaruhi penyakit periodontal dan pembentukan biofilm yang berkontribusi pada pengembangan karies akar.

There is also a link between smoking and periodontal disease and caries, as smoking triggers the formation of plaque and biofilm (i.e., the etiologies of periodontal disease and caries). According to our regression analysis, participants who drank alcohol had significantly higher levels of RC; however, descriptively, non-alcohol drinkers tended to have higher levels of RC. In one study from China, drinking alcohol was found to be significantly correlated with increased rates of RC in a bivariate test but not in multivariate tests; 11 however, a study and review from Spain showed the opposite result, with no association between drinking alcohol and RC. 19 Alcohol use exerts a direct biological effect on the oral cavity by altering salivary flow rate, pH value, and colonization of sub- and supragingival plaque bacterial species, as well as interfering with the immune system of the host.

20 However, this effect could be minimized with behaviors accompanying it to maintain good oral health, such as brushing teeth, which can reduce dental plaque. Our findings support this claim, as those who did not regularly brush their teeth were at greater risk of RC. Although sugar is one of the main factors in the occurrence of caries, in our study, the correlation between the behaviors of drinking and eating sweets and caries development was not statistically significant, similar to other studies conducted in Bogotá, Colombia. 21 Our study found that drinking soda was significantly associated with RC in multivariable analysis, but descriptively, respondents who did not drink soda tended to have more RC. The risk of carbonated beverages comes from their relatively high sucrose concentration, which can induce the formation of biofilms. 19 Most of our study participants did not drink soda.

The occurrence of RC in non-soda drinkers may be caused by other factors, such as brushing behavior, as well as the condition of the gingiva and periodontal tissue. Respondents who chewed betel had relatively more RC. Descriptively, >50% of users of chewed betel had RC. Previous research found relationships between betel chewing and the incidence of coronal caries, 22 affected periodontitis, and bone loss. 8 Although chewing betel has an anti-cariogenic effect due to betel quid’s high fluoride content and etheric oils, it also harms periodontal tissue owing to the cholinergic impact of betel quid combined with calcium salt in the saliva, which produces calculus deposition. Heavy calculus deposition can induce the destruction of gingival tissue and the periodontal membrane.

Potongan ini mendeskripsikan hubungan kompleks antara kondisi periodontal (termasuk bleeding on probing dan attachment loss), gingival recession, dan peningkatan risiko root caries berdasarkan bukti epidemiologi dari berbagai penelitian internasional.

8,12 Chewing betel indirectly affects the occurrence of RC through the gingival and periodontal tissue, as patients with gingival or periodontal disease are at greater risk of developing RC. Our study found that those with BOP (+) and >3 mm of attachment loss had an increased rate of RC. A separate review stated that clinical attachment loss and gingival recession are predisposing factors for RC, given the increased susceptibility of the exposed root surface. 23 Root caries generally presents as a progressive lesion found on the root of a tooth that, due to some degree of periodontal attachment loss, has been exposed to the oral environment. Studies from three different regions—England, Northern Ireland, and Wales—found that individuals with periodontitis had more coronal caries and RC. 24 Although erosive tooth wear and dental caries differ in their causes, both are mediated by diet.

Potongan ini menjelaskan mekanisme biologis dan faktor desain yang mendasari mengapa kondisi-kondisi tertentu meningkatkan kerentanan terhadap karies akar di antara responden yang diperiksa.
text:
Ireland, and Wales—found that individuals with periodontitis had more coronal caries and RC. 24 Although erosive tooth wear and dental caries differ in their causes, both are mediated by diet.

Therefore, dietary behavioral surveys can also be applied when assessing dental caries experience. 25 The current study found that erosion is associated with RC. Studies on adults in Norway 26 reported a correlation between erosion and dental caries, although they did not specifically analyze the correlation with RC. The opposite effect was observed in studies on adults in Finland. 25 Our results showed that people with dentures had significantly higher rates of RC. A study in Ireland found that wearing dentures was significantly associated with RC in univariate tests but not significant in multivariate tests or the final prediction model. 27 The effect of dentures on caries incidence is influenced by the design and type of materials used. Removable dentures have the potential to change the oral environment and increase the formation of plaque on the tooth surface covered by dentures.

Potongan menjelaskan mekanisme bagaimana protesa gigi meningkatkan risiko karies serta menguraikan strategi multi-sektor yang diperlukan untuk mengurangi beban penyakit karies melalui edukasi kesehatan gigi dan kolaborasi antara lembaga pendidikan dan kesehatan.

28 Studies have shown that fixed and removable dentures increase biofilm formation and the risk of caries, gingivitis, and periodontal disease. 28 Based on the results of this study, it is necessary to make systematic and collective efforts between various sectors (i.e., individual, private, and government) to reduce the caries burden in all age groups. 29 Increasing knowledge and self-efficacy through health education in schools in collaboration with dental professionals is critical to maintaining oral health early so that coronal caries and RC can be prevented in old age. 30 This plan requires collaboration between the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Health to create a synergistic curriculum. Dental professionals must be aware of the importance of early detection and prevention of RC, so its associated morbidity rate can be reduced.

Therefore, it is necessary to conduct an in-depth study on causality factors of RC using a longitudinal study design. To conclude, the prevalence of RCs in Indonesia is relatively high; many occur in older adults, and most are not treated. Many different factors contribute to RC in the Indonesian adult population, including sociodemography, oral health practices, general health behaviors, and oral health status. Most of the respondents are young adults; therefore, in the next few years, the number of older adults will increase. Health behaviors that pose a risk of causing RC are still quite high among respondents, including smoking and visiting the dentist. The oral health conditions of respondents that influenced the occurrence of RC were found to be quite high, especially those related to periodontal conditions.

context: Potongan ini adalah bagian pengantar dari sebuah policy brief yang menganalisis profil epidemiologis early childhood caries (karies anak usia dini) di Indonesia dengan membandingkan kesuksesan program kesehatan gigi pada anak usia sekolah terhadap prevalensi tinggi karies pada anak prasekolah. Artikel ini ditulis oleh peneliti dari Universitas Gadjah Mada dan bertujuan memahami hubungan antara epidemiologi ECC dan komponen pembangunan kesehatan untuk merumuskan kebijakan yang tepat.

Many posi tive results have been achieved, which indicate an increasing number of school-ag ed children free of caries and a decrease in caries experience scores. However, result of previous studies on early childhood caries (ECC) in pre-school children showed high prevalence and severity. Understanding the link between the epidemiology of the ECC a nd components of health development is critical for formulating appropriate actio ns.

Potongan ini memperkenalkan masalah kesehatan gigi masyarakat yang akan dianalisis lebih lanjut dalam konteks kebijakan kesehatan Indonesia dan ketersediaan tenaga kesehatan gigi.

The purpose of this study is to provide a comprehensive review of the epidemiology of ECC in Indonesia based on the results of the national basic health surveys. The complemen tary data describes access, utilization and proﬁle of oral health personnel in Indonesi a. Keywords: early childhood caries, Indonesia, caries, poli cy, children INTRODUCTION Dental caries aﬀects people of all ages and remains the major probl em of dental health among children worldwide ( 1). For preschool children, early childhood caries (ECC) deﬁne d as the presence of one or more decayed (non-cavitated or cavitated l esions), missing (due to caries) or ﬁlled tooth surfaces in any primary tooth in children <71 months of age ( 2). ECC is highly prevalent ( 3), associated with multiple risk factor ( 4), and reduces the quality of life ( 5).

If ECC treatment is delayed, the condition of the child worsens and becomes harder to treat, increasing the treatment cost. ECC is also highly prevalence in preschool children living in developing countries like Indonesia (6). Every 5 years, the Indonesian government conducts basic h ealth surveillance. There are surveillance reports on oral health and caries in children fo r the years 2007, 2013 and 2018 ( 7–9). Unfortunately, direct comparison of data is diﬃcult because t he reporting format is not in a same manner for each year. This study will therefore be limited to acomprehensive review of the available data on ECC accessible from the basic health surveillance repor ts, and data from the scientiﬁc publications on ECC in Indonesia. Situational analysis of ora l health services in Indonesia will also be explored.

First, it suggests that prevalence of ECC is increasing over the stud y period, and second, it suggests that children age 3–4 years contribute signiﬁcantly to the high prevalence of ECC in the country. Caries severity also appears to increase by almost a third between the ages 3–4 and 5 years. Publications on ECC in Indonesia has been limited in scope. Most of them were conducted in cities with few participants. In 1992, a study on preschool-aged children in the Jakarta are a showed an ECC prevalence of 85.17% ( 10). Other research on ECC conducted in Jakarta in 2001 and 2008 reported prevalence of 81.2% ( 11) and 80.95% ( 12), respectively. context: Bagian ini merangkum temuan dari berbagai studi publikasi ilmiah tentang prevalensi Early Childhood Caries (ECC) di berbagai wilayah Indonesia, menunjukkan variasi geografis yang signifikan dan mengidentifikasi faktor risiko utama seperti pendidikan maternal, pengetahuan oral health, dan perilaku kebersihan gigi. Data ini melengkapi analisis epidemiologis dari survei kesehatan nasional dengan bukti dari penelitian lokal di Jakarta, Jawa, Yogyakarta, Kalimantan Selatan, dan Sulawesi Utara.

Lower prevalence were reported in studies conducted in West and East Java; in West Java ECC prevalence was 70% ( 13) while it was 42.9% or children aged 3 years in East Java. The prevalence of severe ECC was 57.1% in East Java ( 14). Caries prevalence of 94.3% was reported in 4– 6 year old children in Yogyakarta ( 15), and a prevalence of 100 and 88.5% reported in 5-year-olds resident in South Kalimant an and North Sulawesi, respectively ( 16, 17). Identiﬁed risk factors for ECC studies in Indonesia include low maternal education ( 12, 15), poor maternal knowledge of oral health ( 13, 16), and consumption of cariogenic foods, which had a signiﬁcant relationship with the severity of ECC ( 12). Children who do not brush their teeth regularly from an early age also had high ris k of ECC (15).

Penekanan pada keragaman etnis, budaya, dan bahasa Indonesia menjadi latar belakang untuk memahami disparitas dalam kesehatan oral anak-anak pra sekolah antar pulau dan kelompok populasi.

Socio-Demographic Context Indonesia is an archipelago state which is located between two continents (Asia and Australia) and two oceans (Indian and Paciﬁc). The width of land area in Indonesia is around 1,916,862.2 km 2, while the width of its sea is about 3,257,483 km2. Indonesia is a country with the fourth largest population worldwide ( 18). Indonesian people are comprised of many ethnics and cultures. There are more than 700 local languages and dialects in the daily life of its people ( 19). It is evident that variations in caries prevalence among children are associated with multiple factors, including eth nicity and culture. Results of national basic health surveys in Indo nesia also show that prevalence and severity of oral disease varies across ethnic groups. DISCUSSION It is evident that the number of ECC studies carried out in Indonesia over the last 20 years is limited, yet in general the data generated consistently shows high prevalen ce. Methodological diﬀerences and confounding factors, especial ly socio-demographic inﬂuences, limit national comparisons of data on caries prevalence. The increasing number of oral health personnel, along with the increase in the per-capita expenditure toward health servi ces, does not seem to have had a signiﬁcant impact. However, the decision maker (e.g., district health oﬃce) need to realize that the chosen strategic model to tackle ECC cannot be separated from the socio-economic context.

Therefore, dental caries in prescho olers can be expected to increase in coming years. In this case, successful cases of sugar restrictions policy in other count ries could serve as examples of the importance of continuous oral health promotion ( 33). Sociodemographic variations can be a signiﬁcant barrier, especially in low-income and low-education populations, and can have an impact on low awareness of the importance of oral health for children. This condition must be an alarm fo r policy makers because the current best practices for reducing the risk of ECC include twice-daily brushing with ﬂuoridate d tooth paste.

ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS Taken together, the results of analysis on epidemiological d ata and oral health policy suggest following recommendations: • National preventive program toward ECC should be prioritized including activity of prevention program in kindergarten or early childhood education. However, oral health programs for young children cannot rely solely on school-based and the decision maker must consider a reasonable range of alternatives to expand the provision of the program. • Expanding the program via maternal care should be considered as a potential alternative. Integrating immunization programs with dental check-ups also could be another option, since this program is widely spread and accepted among citizen. • Oral health training can be provided for other health workers , like midwives, to help them identify, and refer high-risk patients for subsequent care management in a dental clinic.

Potongan ini merangkum kesimpulan utama bahwa diperlukan revisi menyeluruh terhadap kebijakan kesehatan gigi masyarakat untuk mencegah prevalensi ECC yang tinggi pada anak usia dini di Indonesia.

among citizen. • Oral health training can be provided for other health workers , like midwives, to help them identify, and refer high-risk patients for subsequent care management in a dental clinic.

Such programs should be actively delivered via early childhood education programs by involving teachers and health cadres via integrated healthcare posts. • Under the NHI system, there is a potential scheme in implementing early screening for ECC for pre-schoolers. Children referred upon screening will be treated free of char ge in CHCs. • National data on caries should illustrate the prevalence for each of the provinces to indicate regional diﬀerences. If the decision maker seeks to develop an eﬃcient and sustainable oral health system, the successes, and failures of the existi ng service model must be identiﬁed. The decision maker needs to realize that the chosen strategic model to tackle ECC cannot be separated from the socio-economic context. CONCLUSION There is a necessity to review dental public health policies an d develop eﬀective strategies to prevent the epidemic of ECC in Indonesia.

The key to success in the prevention and curative management of ECC lies not only in the availability of oral health personnel but also in a joint commitment with other parties. Further, advocacy to prevent healthcare problems among children is critical because this will have consequences for general health. In particular, policies that promote children ’s oral health as part of public health initiatives can help attra ct people’s attention.
