title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian pendahuluan ini menjabarkan metodologi ulasan naratif komprehensif tentang status dan sistem kesehatan gigi Indonesia selama dekade 2013-2023, dengan pencarian sistematis melalui basis data ilmiah utama dan dokumen pemerintah. Penelitian ini dirancang untuk mengidentifikasi tantangan kesehatan gigi di Indonesia dan merumuskan rekomendasi berdasarkan bukti literatur terkini serta regulasi kesehatan nasional.
text: 352 Aim: To assess the current situation regarding oral health status and system in Indonesia through the existing literature and government documents, identify challenges, and propose recommendations for the future. Materials and Methods: A literature search was conducted from June to October 2023 through the scientific databases of PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, including published articles from 2013 to 2023. The following main keywords were used: “Indonesia,” “oral health system,” “oral healthcare system,” “oral health policy,” “oral health promotion,” “oral health coverage,” and “oral health status.” Articles without any restrictions on study design, review articles, regional or national oral health reports, and Indonesian health laws or regulations were included. Data extracted from the included studies were synthesized and presented into several subgroups.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Potongan ini menyajikan hasil utama dan kesimpulan dari review naratif tentang status kesehatan gigi dan sistem perawatan gigi di Indonesia selama dekade 2013-2023, mengidentifikasi tantangan sistemik utama seperti distribusi tenaga kerja gigi yang tidak merata dan alokasi sumber daya yang tidak memadai dalam mencapai cakupan kesehatan universal. Potongan ini merangkum temuan kunci bahwa meskipun berbagai kebijakan telah diimplementasikan sejak pembentukan sistem kesehatan nasional pada 1982, prevalensi penyakit gigi yang tidak terobati tetap tinggi dan memerlukan tindakan komprehensif di masa depan.
text:
regional or national oral health reports, and Indonesian health laws or regulations were included. Data extracted from the included studies were synthesized and presented into several subgroups.

Results: Despite the establishment of a health system in 1982, the oral health status of Indonesian people remains unsatisfying. The prevalence of untreated caries and periodontal disease is still high. Several policies and programs have been implemented to tackle those problems; however, Indonesia still has many challenges to overcome, including geographic constraints, uneven distribution of dental personnel, low public awareness and information on oral care utilization, insufficient resource allocation, and lack of prevention and promotion programs. Conclusion: The oral health status of the Indonesian population remains unsatisfactory. Future actions should emphasize on equal access and distribution of dental care, strengthen monitoring and evaluation of ongoing programs, integrate oral health into the national health agenda, and allocate adequate resources to support oral health initiatives.

Indonesia launched the NHI scheme, known as Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN), in 2014. The JKN aims to provide basic health services that covers various aspects of healthcare to all Indonesians.

[34] The JKN scheme has enrolled approximately 250 million people, making it one of the largest health insurance schemes in Indonesia. [34] The health insurance budget is managed by BPJS Kesehatan, a single health purchasing agency, and it is financed by the government, employers, employees, and insured individuals. [30] The primary healthcare payment system operates on a capitation basis, where general dentists receive payment for specific health services provided to each registered patient within a defined period. Oral examination, basic treatments, and emergency are covered under this scheme, with advanced treatments referred to specialized healthcare facilities [Supplementary Figure 2]. The Usaha Kesehatan Gigi Sekolah (UKGS) program offers integrated dental healthcare services specifically for elementary and middle schoolaged children, including dental and oral health screening, education, regular checkups, mass toothbrushing initiatives, and advanced dental services.[38] Oral health services for older adults prioritize curative and rehabilitative approaches, aiming to restore masticatory function.

The direction also emphasized on the multidisciplinary approach and educational intervention for the caregivers for the provision of oral health support.[36] dIscussIon To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first comprehensive review of Indonesia’s oral health status and oral healthcare system after the NHI implementation. The most recent National Basic Health Survey in 2018 (Riskesdas) revealed unsatisfying results regarding the oral health status of the population. [9] Despite common oral health issues shared with other countries, Indonesia faces unique challenges in its efforts to improve oral health conditions. This necessitates strengthening oral health conditions, strengthening health systems, and establishing policies addressing oral health needs comprehensively.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian Diskusi review ini menganalisis kesenjangan antara target nasional Indonesia untuk skor DMF-T (decayed, missing, filled teeth) pada anak usia 12 tahun dan status kesehatan mulut yang sebenarnya, dengan menekankan bahwa prevalensi penyakit periodontal tetap tinggi dan akses ke perawatan gigi yang tidak memadai serta topografi geografis yang unik menjadi hambatan utama dalam meningkatkan kesehatan mulut populasi Indonesia.
text:
to improve oral health conditions. This necessitates strengthening oral health conditions, strengthening health systems, and establishing policies addressing oral health needs comprehensively.

According to the National Health Action Plan of Indonesia, the government set the target to achieve the DMF-T score for the 12-year group, that is, 1.14 in 2025, and the long-term target is set to achieve DMF-T 1 in 2030. [40] This target sounds ambitious without any significant effort since the current DMF-T is still exceeding the target, which was around 1.9 at the national level and varied between 1.6 and 3.2 in some previous studies [Supplementary Table 1].[9,10,13,14,17,18,41,42] This is similar to the prevalence of periodontal disease, which is still high, that is, around 19.6% at the national level, and varied between 28% and 100% among different age groups [Supplementary Table 2].[43] Several possible reasons for the oral health status of the underprivileged Indonesian population suggest inadequate access to dental care. The country’s unique topography may also be contributing to these challenges.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian Diskusi ini menganalisis tantangan utama yang dihadapi sistem kesehatan oral Indonesia, khususnya masalah aksesibilitas dan distribusi tenaga kerja gigi yang tidak merata di berbagai wilayah geografis. Potongan ini membandingkan rasio tenaga kesehatan gigi Indonesia dengan standar WHO dan negara-negara Asia Tenggara lainnya, serta menekankan peran penting dental terapis dalam mengatasi kekurangan dokter gigi untuk program pencegahan dan promosi kesehatan oral.
text:
reasons for the oral health status of the underprivileged Indonesian population suggest inadequate access to dental care. The country’s unique topography may also be contributing to these challenges.

Further efforts are needed to sustainably improve access to dental care, with the Ministry of Health taking responsibility and receiving support from other governmental and non-governmental organizations. The role of oral health personnel is crucial; certain regions in Indonesia experience a shortage of dental professionals, resulting in a heavier workload for available health workers. According to the WHO standards, the number of oral health personnel falls below the recommended level, with only 1.2 dentists per 10,000 population in 2021.[44] This is notably lower than the statistics in neighboring countries such as Malaysia (2.9:10,000 in 2018), Thailand (2.5:10,000 in 2019), and the Philippines (2.5:10,000 in 2021).[45] Given the scarcity of dentists in Indonesia, dental therapists are vital in oral healthcare prevention and promotion.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian diskusi ini membandingkan ketersediaan tenaga gigi Indonesia dengan negara-negara tetangga dan membahas tantangan distribusi tenaga kerja gigi serta solusi potensial untuk meningkatkan layanan kesehatan gigi nasional. Potongan ini menekankan peran penting terapis gigi dan profesi kesehatan gigi lainnya dalam mengatasi kekurangan personel gigi terutama di daerah terpencil.
text:
Thailand (2.5:10,000 in 2019), and the Philippines (2.5:10,000 in 2021).[45] Given the scarcity of dentists in Indonesia, dental therapists are vital in oral healthcare prevention and promotion.

However, the uneven distribution of the dentist workforce and dental therapists nationwide results in untreated oral health issues and neglect of preventive measures, particularly in remote areas. To mitigate the shortage of dental personnel for providing preventive care, it may be necessary to introduce people from additional oral healthcare professions such as dental hygiene. Furthermore, national-level implementation of oral health policies is essential to improve oral healthcare services, considering the available dental workforce.

Indonesia’s healthcare facility budget has remained stagnant, hovering between 2.8% and 3.02% of GDP from 2013 to 2019. [46] Although the government has spent more on healthcare-related expenditures in 2023 by about 5.3%, the allocation was mainly to tackle the post-pandemic situation, while also providing for sustaining the NHI scheme. Compared to neighboring countries, Indonesia’s healthcare expenditures are lower than those of other Southeast Asian countries [Supplementary Figure 3].

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian diskusi ini menganalisis tantangan finansial dan aksesibilitas sistem kesehatan gigi Indonesia dalam konteks implementasi asuransi kesehatan nasional (NHI/JKN) sejak 2014 dan program Nusantara Sehat untuk menjangkau daerah terpencil. Potongan ini menekankan kesenjangan antara pengeluaran kesehatan Indonesia yang lebih rendah dibandingkan negara-negara Asia Tenggara lainnya dan kebutuhan akan akses perawatan gigi yang lebih merata untuk semua populasi tanpa memandang lokasi geografis atau status ekonomi.
text:

[46] These financial challenges necessitate thorough assessment, especially considering the ongoing enrollment under the NHI scheme since 2014 and the persistent issue of excessive out-of-pocket expenses despite limited improvement in national health expenditures. While the NHI scheme aims to provide comprehensive healthcare to Indonesians, gaps in coverage or accessibility may exist, particularly for rural populations. Despite the implementation of the Nusantara Sehat program in 2015 to address this issue, significant improvements have yet to be observed. [23] Efforts should be made to ensure equitable access to dental care services for all Indonesians, regardless of the location or socioeconomic status. This may involve expanding the network of covered healthcare facilities and improving the infrastructure in underserved areas.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian diskusi ini membahas rekomendasi untuk mengatasi kesenjangan akses layanan kesehatan gigi di Indonesia setelah implementasi Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional, sambil mengakui keterbatasan penelitian karena tidak tersedianya data survei kesehatan mulut terbaru sejak tahun 2018.
text:

Additionally, utilizing digital or teledentistry to address these issues may be feasible with available technological resources and internet coverage. Despite oral healthcare services tailored to various life stages, accessibility remains challenging. While programs prioritize preventive approaches, gaps in implementation exist. Emphasizing preventive measures such as regular checkups, oral hygiene education, and early intervention strategies could help mitigate oral health problems. Programs in Indonesia target specific age groups, but there is a lack of emphasis on early childhood care. This review has some limitations. The lack of recent oral health survey data, unavailable since 2018, significantly restricts the analysis.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian diskusi ini merangkum keterbatasan metodologis dari review naratif tentang status kesehatan gigi dan sistem perawatan gigi Indonesia, termasuk kurangnya data survei terbaru sejak 2018 dan laporan evaluasi komprehensif program pencegahan. Penulis menekankan bahwa meskipun dengan keterbatasan tersebut, review memberikan wawasan penting untuk mengembangkan kebijakan kesehatan gigi yang lebih baik dan meningkatkan akses ke layanan perawatan gigi terutama di daerah terpencil melalui integrasi prioritas kesehatan gigi dalam agenda kesehatan nasional Indonesia.
text:
but there is a lack of emphasis on early childhood care. This review has some limitations. The lack of recent oral health survey data, unavailable since 2018, significantly restricts the analysis.

Consequently, the research findings may not fully capture the country’s oral health status since most regulations governing the national oral healthcare system are managed within the broader healthcare framework. The absence of comprehensive evaluation reports on oral health systems and prevention programs makes it challenging to evaluate the successful rate of the programs. Nevertheless, this review offers essential and updated insights to inform better oral health policies and set specific goals for oral health promotion in Indonesia. There is a need to strengthen access to oral healthcare services, particularly in remote areas, through collaborative efforts in Indonesia. By prioritizing oral healthcare within national health agendas and implementing evidence-based strategies, Indonesia can work toward achieving better oral health outcomes for its population.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian penutup review ini merangkum rekomendasi utama untuk meningkatkan status kesehatan gigi Indonesia, menekankan perlunya integrasi kesehatan gigi dalam agenda kesehatan nasional, penguatan perawatan primer, dan peningkatan kapasitas tenaga kerja. Potongan ini menyimpulkan bahwa meskipun prevalensi karies gigi dan penyakit periodontal tetap tinggi dan melampaui target nasional DMF-T, strategi berbasis bukti dan prioritas pencegahan dapat membantu Indonesia mencapai hasil kesehatan gigi yang lebih baik.
text:
By prioritizing oral healthcare within national health agendas and implementing evidence-based strategies, Indonesia can work toward achieving better oral health outcomes for its population.

In conclusion, the high prevalence of dental caries and periodontal diseases, as well as DMF-T, which is considerably higher than the national target, suggests that the oral health status of Indonesian people remains dissatisfying. To overcome that situation, strengthening primary care and its ongoing programs, prioritizing oral health with emphasis on preventive measures in the national agenda, enhancing workforce capacity, and promoting preventive measures are crucial steps for future directions. acknowledgment We would like to express gratitude to the Department of Preventive and Community Dentistry, Faculty of Dentistry, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Y ogyakarta, Indonesia, and also Department of Dental Public Health, Universitas Airlangga, Surabaya, Indonesia, for their collaboration. financial Support and SponSorShip This study was funded by Heiwa Nakajima Foundation in 2024. conflictS of intereSt Nil.

title: Oral health status and system in Indonesia: a review
context: Bagian ini menjelaskan komponen life-course oral healthcare services yang diimplementasikan oleh Kementerian Kesehatan Indonesia pada tahun 2015, mencakup target populasi spesifik (ibu hamil, anak-anak, lansia, dan individu dengan kebutuhan khusus), lokasi layanan, dan pendekatan perawatan yang disesuaikan dengan setiap kelompok usia. Potongan ini menunjukkan strategi Indonesia untuk mengintegrasikan perawatan gigi ke dalam sistem kesehatan primer melalui berbagai fasilitas kesehatan masyarakat.
text:
and to prevent congenital diseases, particularly in the oro-facial region. This kind of dental care focuses on promotive and preventive approaches without neglecting curative and rehabilitative care.

Dental and oral healthcare services for the older adults are prioritized on services with a curative and rehabilitative approach in the form of treatment and restoration of masticatory function according to dental and oral health problems in the older adults. Dental and oral health services for individuals with special needs are carried out in accordance with the developmental phases of individuals with disabilities and/or treatment modifications according to the type of disability, level of disability, and whether there are any complications. Location Primary healthcare center (Puskesmas) Primary healthcare center (Puskemas), Integrated Healthcare Center (Posyandu), preschools group, and schools. Primary healthcare centers (Puskemas) and other places provide oral healthcare for the community.

healthcare center (Puskemas), Integrated Healthcare Center (Posyandu), preschools group, and schools. Primary healthcare centers (Puskemas) and other places provide oral healthcare for the community.

Health service facilities that provide dental and oral health services are equipped with special facilities and infrastructure for dental and oral care for persons with disabilities. Service provider The dentist or primary healthcare center’s cadres. Medical personnel, primary healthcare center’s cadres, teachers, and caregivers. Specialist dentists, general dentists, and dental therapists. Activities Dental and oral health services for pregnant women are carried out integrated with the antenatal examination of pregnant women since the first antenatal visit (K1) in the primary healthcare center (Puskesmas). 1.Oral health counseling. 2.Oral health screening and early detection. 3.Referral to the specialist dentist for further curative treatment indications. 1.For infants, toddlers, and pre-school children, dental care is given to the parents or caregivers, such as dental counseling and oral hygiene training.
